appearance_facts.fact: A single pie chart occupies the central area beneath the title.
A pale yellow wedge labeled 'Nuclear (40%)' spans from the top vertical radius down to the left, forming the largest angular slice.
An orange wedge labeled 'Fossil Fuels (15%)' is the smallest slice, bounded by the top vertical radius and a radius toward the lower right.
A dark red wedge labeled 'Hydroelectric (25%)' sits between the yellow and orange-red slices.
An orange-red wedge labeled 'Renewables (20%)' fills the bottom-right region.

printed_facts.fact: Title reads 'Global Energy Consumption by Source'.
Percentages sum to 100% (40 + 15 + 25 + 20); no separate axis, legend, or unit scale is printed.

public_definitions: Routing criterion: 'Largest global energy consumption category'.
uncertain: The chart uses stylized percentages that do not match real-world global energy data; the decision must rely solely on the printed labels, which are internally consistent.
